qualification.independently_recomputed: Four WAT source hashes and operation counts; eight AOT SHA-256 and lengths; 64 timing rows and medians/ratios; two quotient-only AOT byte-identity controls; finite-check count receipts

cost_metric: On one Ubuntu 24.04 x86_64 GitHub runner, end-to-end Wasmtime CLI subprocess compile+serialize elapsed wall time; includes startup, frontend, compiler and AOT serialization; eight per compiler per case; alternating ABBA/BAAB for four cycles
diagnostic: The patched compiler calls a structural verifier on every optimized x86-64 function, including the quotient-only negative control whose AOT bytes remain identical. The control's apparent 7-8% end-to-end compile-time regression is consistent with verifier overhead but not isolated causally; a conditional-verifier A/B on the same host would test this hypothesis.
limits: Artificial modules comprise 64 or 256 copies of one simple exported function; not representative applications
One shared CI virtual machine, eight samples per compiler/fixture, exploratory timing only
Observed whole-AOT size deltas are not CLIF costs, x86 instruction-byte counts, or native throughput
The two compiler binaries are source- and SHA-256-pinned to the archived post-Souper producer run; no upstream branch was modified
Finite native arithmetic/trap observations and prior separate SMT/CLIF checks do not prove compiler-pass/ISA/flags/poison correctness
No new synthesis-discovered sequence; the evaluated div/rem combiner is human-authored
Full proof of cross-target compiler semantics and representative profitability remain outstanding
